*Operational playbook for the broad Phase II reset after the failed narrow W4-B diagnostic.*

<!-- MM:BEGIN:DOCBODY -->

# 1. Purpose

This playbook tells coding agents and reviewers what to do next. It is not a production manual.

# 2. Current active lane

```text
Active lane:     Phase II Broad Reset
Sequence:        P2-MAP -> P2-MATRIX -> P2-NARROW -> P2-PORTFOLIO
Previous lanes:  W3-A (closed)
                 W3-B (closed)
                 W3-C (closed)
                 W3-D (stopped / deferred)
                 W4-A (diagnostic)
                 W4-B (failed narrow diagnostic)
```

The W3 router is a recent-winner child-policy selector, not a learned router. The first narrow W4-B learned-router attempt failed primary success; do not treat that as a final rejection of broad routing or adaptation.

# 3. Execution rule

Current work asks whether a broad candidate matrix can produce controlled survivors. Do not:

- patch the recent-winner router;
- rerun one narrow Elastic Net / Ridge / XGBoost router variant as the whole plan;
- tune the failed child-level liquidity penalty;
- resume W3-D replay debugging, unless a survivor needs Surface D attribution and W3-B re-emits validated row-level decisions;
- claim tradable alpha;
- jump to portfolio expression before P2-NARROW classifies at least one survivor.

# 4. Lessons carried into the broad Phase II reset

## 4.1 Emit row-level decisions at run time

W3-D was stopped because post-hoc row-level reconstruction did not match frozen utilities. Replay drift invalidates downstream mechanism classification.

Rule: any lane whose results may later require row-level attribution must emit immutable row-level selected decisions at run time. Aggregates must reproduce report-level utilities before any attribution analysis runs.

## 4.2 Recent-winner selection is a weak baseline

The W3 router picked among child policies based on prior or recent child-policy performance. It did not train a model over row-level market features.

Rule: do not spend lanes optimizing a recent-winner heuristic. Treat it as a baseline only. Future router work must be separately scoped, must include an oracle-opportunity audit, and must train a real gating model with a credible feature surface beyond recent winners.

## 4.3 Liquidity belongs in the portfolio layer

W3-C's child-level liquidity score-time penalty damaged the clean surface without improving the liquidity surface.

Rule: liquidity treatment for survivor candidates belongs in P2-PORTFOLIO — position caps, capacity caps, exposure shaping — not in child-level score multiplication.

## 4.4 Concentration is a portfolio question

Multiple lanes flagged concentration: W2-v2 was top-contributor dependent, and W3-B's clean-surface gains weakened or reversed under top-contributor stress.

Rule: P2-NARROW and P2-PORTFOLIO must evaluate top-k contributor stress, regime exposure share, and capacity curves as first-class metrics, not appendix material.

# 5. Broad reset order of operations

1. Emit `architecture_map`: data surfaces, markets, feature families, blocked inputs, model families, router targets, decision rules, comparators, and portfolio constraints.
2. Emit `model_family_registry`, `signal_family_registry`, and `surface_market_registry`.
3. Build `candidate_matrix` across Ridge, Elastic Net, Bayesian Ridge, Bayesian LASSO / sparse Bayesian proxy, Group LASSO, Sparse Group LASSO, PCR / PLS, XGBoost, Random Forest / ExtraTrees, quantile regression, contextual bandit, and mixture-of-experts. Treat MAML / Reptile-style adaptation as later-stage.
4. For each candidate, bind router target and decision rule: child utility regression, utility distribution, pairwise advantage, override probability, abstain probability, regime classifier plus policy map; free routing, default override, confidence-bound override, Thompson-style sampling, risk-adjusted expected utility, or drawdown-aware selection.
5. Validate PIT, leakage, provenance, split, feature allowlist, and forbidden hindsight columns.
6. Run P2-NARROW against baseline uplift, robustness, concentration, liquidity, cost, drawdown, and falsification checks.
7. Emit `narrowing_report` and `survivor_manifest`.
8. Run portfolio expression only for candidates classified `SURVIVOR_READY_FOR_PORTFOLIO`.

# 6. Failure handling

| Failure | Response |
|---|---|
| Aggregated row-level decisions do not reproduce report utilities | Mark candidate inconclusive; re-emit before reclassifying |
| Candidate fails best-child baseline | Classify `NARROWED_OUT_BASELINE`; do not rescue with post-hoc thresholds |
| Candidate fails robustness, leakage, concentration, liquidity, cost, drawdown, or falsification | Classify `NARROWED_OUT_ROBUSTNESS` or the closest explicit failure label |
| Candidate is another narrow W4-B style rerun | Classify `FAILED_NARROW_DIAGNOSTIC` unless it belongs to a declared matrix cell |
| All candidates narrow out | Stop before portfolio expression and record the controlled negative result |
| Portfolio survives only after uncontrolled rule changes | Invalid; rerun through P2-NARROW |

# 7. Deferred and paused work

| Item | Status | Resume condition |
|---|---|---|
| W3-D mechanism audit | Stopped / deferred | A survivor needs Surface D attribution and W3-B emits validated row-level selected decisions |
| Additional liquidity-penalty variants | Paused | Not the right layer; revisit only if survivor portfolio treatment proves insufficient |
| Recent-winner router optimization | Closed | Future router work belongs in the broad matrix, not recent-winner tuning |
| Later-stage adaptation | Deferred | Simpler model families leave residual opportunity after controlled narrowing |

# 8. Interpretation rules

## 8.1 Raw diagnostic surface

Diagnostic only. Not a basis for alpha claims.

## 8.2 Clean primary surface

The main W4 evaluation surface, using the repaired definition.

## 8.3 Winsorized sensitivity surface

Sensitivity context only. Strong results here do not override liquidity-surface failure.

## 8.4 Liquidity / tradability surface

A W4 candidate that fails on this surface should classify as a liquidity / capacity failure unless the portfolio layer absorbs the constraint via caps.

## 8.5 Concentration stress surfaces

A W4 candidate that depends on top contributors should classify as a concentration failure even if the clean-surface utility is otherwise positive.

# 9. Router-language enforcement

| Use | Avoid |
|---|---|
| recent-winner router | learned meta-router |
| recent-winner child-policy selector | adaptive meta-router |
| weak baseline router | meta-learning router |
| recent-winner heuristic | true gating model |
|  | Reptile router |
|  | ML router |

Any agent output that describes the current router as a learned router is a documentation defect and must be corrected.

# 10. Agent output expectations

Every agent output should say what was changed, what was not changed, commands run, artifacts emitted, blocked PIT-safe inputs, whether row-level decisions were emitted and validated where applicable, which P2 narrowing or W4 portfolio classification was reached where applicable, and the next recommended action.

# 11. Keep scope tight

Do not add during broad Phase II reset unless admitted into P2-MAP / P2-MATRIX:

- production control flow;
- broker integration;
- paper trading;
- live trading;
- new complex learners as first-pass router (Reptile, MAML, RL);
- W3-D replay debugging;
- additional child-level liquidity penalties;
- new lanes labelled W3-* (W3 is closed).
